Actually the verifier: panels(across) splits by columns of width = h. So each panel is h x h. For the example: h=3, w=9, so 3 panels of 3x3.

Panel 2 shape = {(0,2),(1,1),(1,2),(2,0),(2,2)}

Panels 1 and 2 share the same shape, panel 0 is odd. Output = panel 0. Good.

So the rule: find the odd panel (the one whose filled-cell shape is unique).

Natural language rule text mentions "most spaces colored" which is misleading but the verifier is what matters. Actually wait—maybe the "most spaces colored" refers to... hmm. The verifier picks the panel whose shape appears once. The panel 0 has 6 filled cells, panels 1,2 have 5. So odd one out has most cells. Either heuristic works. But rule is: unique shape.

Now I need to create demonstration inputs. The verifier requires: run % side == 0, run//side >= 3, and exactly one odd panel with len(tally)==2.

So I need to design 3+ panels, each h x h, where shapes: one shape appears once (the odd), and the other shape appears multiple times. Total distinct shapes == 2. Exactly one unique.
